subject: Econ firebreaks & MAP close timeline — token sensitivity and caching/batching checks
messages:

Subject: Re: Next steps for MAP & pilot economics

Elliot — thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to capture the financial guardrails before we escalate to legal.

Quick background: our clinical triage flow will make ~120k inference calls/day in steady state. Avg payload ~320 tokens in, ~160 tokens out. We need to understand practical tokens/$ under realistic batching and cache assumptions to commit to a pilot start date (target: Dec 6).

Questions we need answered this week: 
- Expected tokens per USD at pilot throughput with 95th %ile latency <= 250ms
- How much benefit do we see with prefix/KV caching for our kind of short dialog patterns (we have ~45% repeat prefixes by session)
- If batching pushes latency above 250ms, what are fallback options in Redwood (smaller batch, live fallback to smaller model, or hosted burst)?

I've attached a short template for the MAP items procurement wants filled out (aperture_map_template.xlsx) — happy to iterate.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Ortiz
VP Product, Aperture Health
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps for MAP & pilot economics

Dana — appreciate the clarity. I pulled an initial pass for the MAP economics and a short list of "firebreaks" (thresholds where we pause rollout or require re-eval). High-level answers below; I'm attaching a draft MAP workbook with assumptions.

Summary (pilot steady state, hosted API, mixed caching + batching):
- Baseline tokens per USD (no caching, moderate batching): ~11,000 tokens/$ at 8-token latency-optimized pricing tier (this is a conservative blended estimate).
- With prefix/KV caching (assume 45% prefix hit, 60% KV reuse on repeats) we estimate effective tokens/$ increases to ~17,000 tokens/$.
- Batching: end-to-end latency at batch size 8 (our runtime profile) is ~180–230ms p95 for your token profile. Batch size 16 pushes p95 above 300ms for some model variants.

Firebreaks (proposed):
1) Latency firebreak: if p95 > 300ms for >5% of peak windows, switch to reduced batching and enable an immediate canary to a lower-latency model.
2) Cost firebreak: if projected monthly token spend deviates >20% from MAP forecast and we can't identify caching/traffic levers, pause expansion and run a 48h sampling window for re-estimation.
3) Quality/degeneration: if automated evals on the MAP prompt set show >2% regression in critical metrics, fallback to prior model version and pause new rollouts.

Ask from us to finalize numbers: upload a 7-day sample of request traces (anonymized) and confirm whether the 45% prefix repeat assumption holds across IDS/sessions. We'll run a short simulation and return a sensitivity matrix (tokens/$ vs caching hit rate vs batch size) by EOD 11/19.

Next steps:
- Dana — can procurement upload a sample trace to the Drive link I sent?
- Marissa — I'll need the sensitivity sheet populated with quantization and Dedicated vs Hosted multipliers.
- Rishi — please review the firebreak thresholds and suggest any contractual language that maps to SLAs/SLOs.

Elliot
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: aperture_map_draft.xlsx

Adding a bit more color — I've run a sensitivity pass and populated the attached unit_econ_sensitivity.csv in the Drive link. High-level notes: 

Assumptions used (documented in sheet):
- Model variant: rdx-2.7b-opt (our typical pilot baseline)
- Per-token pricing (hosted list): $0.00009 per token gen, $0.00003 per token input (blended as $0.00007/token for mixed io)
- Quantization benefit: int8 profiles reduce GPU vram/throughput cost by ~20% on our runtime for this model (less helpful for very short contexts)
- Caching assumptions: prefix hit = 45% (your number). We break caching benefit into prefix-hit (avoids full forward) and KV reuse (avoids recomputing decoder steps) — combined effective token reduction: 37%
- Batching trade-offs: batch=8 is our operational sweet spot for latency <= 250ms p95; batch=16 gives ~22% ops cost reduction but increases p95 beyond your 250ms target in 30% of simulated windows.

Concrete asks for the MAP doc we need to close: 
- Milestone 1 (Pilot signoff): agree on 7-day sampling window, threshold values for firebreaks, and legal's acceptance of the latency remediation steps.
- Milestone 2 (Pilot to Prod): define committed QPS or commit to a dedicated capacity band with monthly commit (if you want predictable unit econ).
- Finance ask: Aperture to confirm whether they require monthly invoicing cadence vs net-30. This changes our recommended commit cadence and the discount schedule.

Practical recommendation: start pilot on hosted with batch=8 + prefix cache enabled. Capture telemetry for 7 days, run our sensitivity matrix, and then decide whether to move to a Dedicated reservation for month 2 (reduces token cost by estimated 15–25% depending on commit).

Attachment listed in Drive: unit_econ_sensitivity.csv (contains scenario grid and sensitivity heatmap).

Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement/engineering review: 

1) The 45% prefix repeat is an org-level average. For triage sessions it spikes to ~65% after intents are detected. We will send a masked trace that highlights session boundaries.
2) We are open to a dedicated commit if the math lines up; procurement will need a 30/60/90 day cadence comparison and the actual projected monthly spend from your sensitivity sheet.
3) Two asks from our infra team: what happens if batch tuning causes jitter (spiky latencies) — will Redwood provide a short-term capacity bump or a contract-level remediation during the pilot window?

Proposed next step: we can share the 7-day sample by EOD 11/19. Can you commit to returning the sensitivity matrix with dedicated vs hosted columns by 11/20 EOD? If so we can keep the Dec 6 pilot start target.

—Dana
